title: StakeWise vaults, Index Coop and reward authority on PulseChain
text:
Appendix 64: StakeWise vaults, Index Coop and
reward authority on PulseChain
Contents of this appendix
dsETH accepts the existing sETH2 identity .............................................................................................................. 411
Is dsETH already controlled by the group? .............................................................................................................. 412
wsETH2, Opium and Babylon ................................................................................................................................... 414
Original reward oracle and distributor ..................................................................................................................... 414
Evidence and reproduction ...................................................................................................................................... 415
Source record: docs/studies/analysis/pulsechain_stakewise_vault_integrations_20261002.md.
StakeWise vaults, Index Coop and reward authority on PulseChain
2 October 2026. Read-only evidence at PulseChain block 27,690,565, hash 
0x8eafcc2cbd9f3c7fd00a499ba4173ba098bc207762d553543f998be5bac03334, timestamp 01:24:15 UTC. Inherited-state
comparisons use block 17,232,999. No transactions, signatures or setter simulations were submitted.
The strongest additional integration is dsETH: it already holds exact sETH2 and has an
installed rETH2 reinvestment extension. Group control of dsETH is not established. Opium and
Babylon add options and investment-strategy routes. The original StakeWise oracle and distributor also
have an administrator already linked to the controlled StakeWise Safe. These findings extend the local
network; none identifies a working L2 bridge.
dsETH accepts the existing sETH2 identity
The copied Index Coop token is dsETH, 0x341c05c0e9b33c0e38d64de76516b2ce970bb3be. Its current components
are:
Component Exact token address Meaning
sETH2 0xfe2e637202056d30016725477c5da089a
b0a043a
Direct StakeWise principal component
wstETH 0x7f39c581f595b53c5cb19bd0b3f8da6c9
35e2ca0
Wrapper for local Lido stETH
rETH 0xae78736cd615f374d3085123a210448e7
4fc6393
Rocket Pool token; different from
StakeWise rETH2
This direct composition agrees with Index Coop's January 2023 explanation. Its earlier launch proposal
discussed wrapping StakeWise exposure; the observed PulseChain basket directly contains sETH2, not
wsETH2. Minting dsETH normally requires the proportional amounts of all three components. Supplying
only newly minted sETH2 does not satisfy that basket.
The installed extension 0x1fcf74d4d0335095c02e1ca78ec55339c2ec927b exactly matches verified Ethereum 
StakeWiseReinvestmentExtension runtime. Its immutable getters identify this dsETH token, exact
sETH2 and exact rETH2. Its configured trade is rETH2 → sETH2, through UniswapV3ExchangeAdapterV2, at fee
tier 500, or 0.05%. It absorbs rETH2 already held by the basket and trades it into principal. reinvest
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 411

requires an allowed caller; anyoneCallable is false, and the three sampled research wallets are not allowed.
The operator can manage that caller list. This is a concrete reward-reinvestment integration, not
arbitrary collateral minting.
At the checkpoint, dsETH supply is 776.8495483. T wo canonical Uniswap V3 dsETH/copied-WETH pools
hold approximately 83.0922 and 827.0058 WETH units on the other side. Copied WETH wraps native
PLS on PulseChain. The checked dsETH/pUSDC pool has zero active liquidity and only 0.000318 pUSDC.
Those balances bound inventory; they are not executable trade quotes or Ethereum redemption rights.
The dsETH issuance-quantity getter currently reverts. Its redemption-quantity getter returns nominal
component amounts, but this does not establish that redemption transfers succeed: sETH2's current
implementation fails ordinary ERC20 getters. Restoring token functionality is necessary for the affected
basket operations.
Is dsETH already controlled by the group?
Not confirmed. Its manager is 0xbb6134ba82192e0ab23de846f1cae7aa9ae383d5, an exact runtime match to
verified BaseManagerV2. Its operator is the Index Coop Engineering Safe, 
0x6904110f17fed2162a11b5fa66b188d801443ea4; its methodologist is the separate contract 
0x8648fefb23b5576c6329cb3514e5cdb54650b0aa. The methodologist's authority was identified through the
manager getter; its internal authorization was not resolved by verified source here.
The Engineering Safe remains 2-of-6, with the same owners, nonce, modules, implementation address,
guard and fallback handler as the fork. Its enabled modules exactly match verified Ethereum runtime:
Module Permission relevant to this investigation
Orca ControllerV1, 
0x4c98af741e352c6551bff9509b3f8ca9dd4e6397

authorized pod administrator can mint or burn

Module Permission relevant to this investigation
AllowanceModule, 
0xcfbfac74c26f8647cbdb8c5caf80bb5b32e43134
Authorizes bounded native/token transfers for registered
delegates; does not expose arbitrary manager calls to
every delegate
Thus unchanged Safe owners alone would be an incomplete check. The actual Orca administrator chain
was followed:
The full root address is 0x9fc7e174e3ad480f3027814f65222726e2f4fe22; the intermediate address is 
0x8c2907b46b386401c2e46903ede0c87d23503159. Their sampled owners, thresholds, enabled modules and Safe
storage match the inherited state. The parent administrator getters also match. The completed selected
post-fork authority-event search returns no events, including after repairing its four membership-
controller query gaps. None of these observed signer lists identifies the sampled 1967, e121 or a8ed
wallets. Those three wallets each hold zero dsETH at the checkpoint; that is not a complete group
holdings census.
The controller's global owner is an Orca PermissionManager, 0x922a37bb4b8a155a916c15c69345731613381870. Its
complete selected role history leaves administrator Safe 0x2c21843f215d17736045d39bad86b68254793193, also 3-
of-5. Its parent pod administrator is another 3-of-5 Safe, 0x945da540ef13bf67dc70ec1670d5352c0c6c8e8f, with
no higher pod administrator. These controls likewise match inherited snapshots. The
PermissionManager's role permits calls as the global contract owner; that is distinct from the per-pod
administrator permission required to change existing pod memberships.
The operator can add extensions and manage unprotected modules through BaseManagerV2.
Consequently, verified control of the Engineering Safe or its membership administrator could open a
portfolio-management route without first replacing the manager. Replacing the manager or altering
protected-module authority requires the source's mutual operator/methodologist approval. The
protected module currently listed is 0x165edf07bb61904f47800e13f5120e64c4b9a186.
Classify dsETH as an existing integration with unproven group control. A demonstrated authorized
execution or evidence linking sufficient live signers or pod-administrator authority to the group would
change that classification. ERC20 holdings alone would not confer manager authority.

wsETH2, Opium and Babylon
wsETH2, 0x5da21d9e63f1ea13d34e48b7223bcc97e3ecd687, is a separate single-component SetT oken: one nominal
sETH2 per basket unit. Its supply is only 0.5439366. Its manager has no extensions, is uninitialized, and
names the Engineering Safe as both operator and methodologist. Its issuance-quantity getter also
reverts. It is an existing wrapper identity, with limited observed use, not an independent ETH reserve or
the current dsETH input.
Opium: StakeWise's June 2022 proposal names three reward-routing contracts. Current code and getters
confirm the seller pool 0x3ee101bf969fac08be892c737d2969b3db38d2b8, named Opium Weekly Turbo sETH2
Seller, whose underlying is exact sETH2. Its LP supply is about 995.3274. The related 
0xd60f0a53c7e97f78fe4ac9013f5749920c601494 exactly matches verified Opium Core runtime; it should not be
counted as another seller vault. The third address is 0xe47b867b2b5b21a2022068c9ef1293783864b274.
Receipt-verified pre-fork events and current flags show all three have StakeWise reward re-routing
enabled. Such re-routing moves staking rewards toward the Merkle distributor; it does not give that
distributor governance of the vault. Options can produce funded premiums, but also create settlement
obligations. Current sETH2 balance calls fail, so usable collateral capacity is unresolved.
Babylon Finance: integration 0x6a2340d167da153f5450ab49073f5155baa56e36 matches the official deployment
artifact after filling its three immutable controller placeholders with 
0xd4a5b5fcb561daf3adf86f8477555b92fba43b5f. Its source stakes native assets through the StakeWise deposit
pool. Its exit converts rETH2 to sETH2 through fee tier 500, then sETH2 to copied WETH through fee tier
3000, and unwraps WETH. The rETH2 leg uses a hard-coded minimum of 98% of nominal input, which
can obstruct a depegged trade.
This establishes a deployed investment-strategy connection. It does not prove a funded active garden,
control of Babylon's controller, or acceptance of arbitrary bridged ERC20s. The upgraded StakeWise
deposit pool and broken sETH2 currently interrupt the original strategy route.
The checked canonical Uniswap V3 factory has one exact rETH2 pool, paired with sETH2 at 
0xa9ffb27d36901f87f1d0f20773f7072e38c5bfba. The three checked V2 factories return 76 unique rETH2 pairs:
2 Uniswap V2, 8 PulseX V1 and 66 PulseX V2. A direct rETH2/WPLS pair holds about 323,023.64 WPLS
against approximately 1.923 billion rETH2. That is a local liquidity connection; it does not value billions
of tokens at Ethereum ETH prices. The full derived pool inventory remains in the evidence directory.
The Yearn discussion is a strategy proposal, not sufficient evidence of a live PulseChain vault. StakeWise
V3/osETH designs launched after the May 2023 fork require separate PulseChain deployment evidence
before inclusion.
Original reward oracle and distributor
The original Merkle distributor is 0xa3f21010e8b9a3930996c8849df38f9ca3647c20; its oracle contract is 
0x8a887282e67ff41d36c0b7537eab035291461acd. Their current implementation runtimes exactly match verified
Ethereum source. Both name the already-controlled StakeWise Safe 
0x144a98cb1cdbb23610501fe6108858d9b7d24934 as their sole enumerated default administrator.
This administrator can change the local oracle roster. The current roster contains five oracle members,
with reward updates requiring signatures from more than two thirds, therefore at least four members.
Neither a8ed nor e121 is currently an oracle member. These are local StakeWise reward/validator-report
signers, not Arbitrum or Optimism rollup validators.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 414

The oracle, rather than an arbitrary admin caller, supplies new distributor roots in the matched
implementation. A valid claim transfers existing funded ERC20s, or invokes the rETH2 claim accounting
against allocated distributor rewards. It does not freely mint arbitrary stablecoins. Local reward
attestations also do not establish Ethereum beacon income or bridge backing.
Three successful direct rETH2 mint transactions parallel the sETH2 issuance already studied: one million,
one trillion and two trillion. Their traces are local a8ed calls through the custom reward-token
implementation, with no bridge or collateral-transfer call. Current nominal total rewards/supply is 
3,000,001,005,828.3261 rETH2, but a8ed's current balance getter returns zero. Historical issuance
must not be presented as proof that a8ed still holds that amount in transferable form.
Evidence and reproduction
Frozen requests, responses, receipts, traces, source extracts and upstream commit references are under 
artifacts/pulsechain-stakewise-integrations-20261002/. Explicit manifests are under Research/experiments/.
Getter batches use Research/scripts/probe_pulsechain_routes.py --block <pinned-block> --calls <manifest> --
output <new-file>; event batches use Research/scripts/collect_pulsechain_events.py --manifest <manifest> --
output <new-file>. Always use the explicit getter manifest; reproductions require fresh output names.
Runtime matching is against deployed bytecode, not token names. Babylon's constructor immutables
are resolved explicitly. V2 and V3 listing retries repair the original factory-query gaps. Positive mint
receipts and traces are verified, while some older rETH2 mint-query ranges still fail across retry batches;
the observed three mints are not claimed to be a complete issuance census. Negative event conclusions
are scoped to the exact queried events, contracts, ranges and completed RPC responses. Getter equality
does not identify private-key holders or exclude off-chain coordination.
python Research/scripts/verify_pulsechain_stakewise_integrations.py --evidence artifacts/pulsechain-stakewise-
integrations-20261002 passed 168 offline evidence checks. These cover snapshot equality, exact
deployed-runtime matches, resolved Babylon immutables, repaired factory and Index membership event
ranges, and mint receipt/trace/header consistency. The run saves verification.json and a SHA-256
inventory of 399 files. They verify saved evidence consistency, while retaining RPC and explorer trust
assumptions.
The earlier lending study (Appendix 39) records Fuse, Silo, Aave, Compound, Balancer and Lido routes
and their separate capacity constraints. This study adds basket management, options, investment
strategies and reward authority to that network.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 415
